prerequisites: Knowledge of basic algebra, mathematical analysis, trigonometry, operations between vectors, gradient operators, divergence and rotor.

Fluid Dynamics content: Fluid properties, Kinematics and fluid dynamics (volumetric and mass flow rate concept), Equation of motion for perfect fluids and Bernoulli equation, Lagrangian and Eulerian point of view and Reynolds transport theorem, Conservation equations (mass, momentum and energy), Laminar and turbulent flow regimes, Flow in the ducts and head losses (Moody's diagram, the boundary layer).

Thermodynamic content: Thermodynamic properties of fluids, and thermodynamic planes, State equation and ideal gas transformations, Principles of thermodynamics for closed systems, Internal energy and enthalpy of the ideal gas, Reversible and irreversible processes.

learning_outcomes.text: To know and understand the fundamental principles of fluid machines operation.
Acquire the knowledge to solve problems related to the operation and use of fluid machines.
Understand the laws of thermodynamic transformations and fluid dynamic processes that occur in fluid machines.
Acquire the skills necessary to perform energy assessments in engineering applications on fluid machines.
Acquire the ability to make hypotheses, assumptions and simplifications of the processes that take place in fluid machines and that involve mass, energy and momentum balances.
Acquire the ability to graphically represent on thermodynamic planes the main transformations associated with the operation of fluid machines and the corresponding thermodynamic cycles they perform.

syllabus_topics: Recall of fluid systems and transformations
Energy conservation laws for closed and open systems
Integral equations for the study of fluid motion
Definition and classification of fluid machines
Definition of total head, available energy, and efficiency
Nozzles and diffusers: form of the ducts and fundamental equations
Critical conditions, design and off-design operating conditions
Absolute and relative systems of reference
Concept of stage and degree of reaction.
Problems of pump operation (characteristic of a circuit, cavitation, etc.)
INTERNAL COMBUSTION ENGINES (ICE) - Overview, classification, structural elements
Cycles of reference for the study of the internal combustion engines
Beau de Rochas and Diesel cycle comparison
Fuels and combustion in the ICE
Torque and power characteristic curves of ICE
teaching_methods: Discussion of photos and schemes of real components
assessment_rules: The examination requires overcoming a written test, consisting of numerical exercises on volumetric machines, turbomachines, and internal combustion engines. To pass the written test, a score higher than 50% of the maximum points is required; this test provides only eligibility for the oral exam. The oral exam, which determines the final evaluation, tests the student's ability to use correct technical terminology, understand physical phenomena governing machine operation, and apply fluid dynamics and thermodynamics laws. The oral exam score is obtained as a sum of scores assigned to three questions (maximum 10 points each), covering the three main areas of the course.
